key_takeaways: These 12 Italy real weddings come from our own pages, grouped by region, with each card drawn only from the couple's published page.
Four of the couples are from Australia, as their pages say: Laura and Wahib, Josh and Isabela, Tiara and Josh, and Loret and Franco.
Several weddings ran over a long weekend: three days for Cristina and Brett in Tuscany and Jenayde and Alfonso in Puglia, and four days of events for Tiara and Josh in Positano.
Ceremonies ranged from a Catholic Mass and a Maronite blessing to a Gujarati Hindu ceremony, and Josh and Isabela held their civil wedding at home in Sydney.
Our Italy timing guide names late May to June and September to early October as the two sweet spots, and our cost guide covers budgets by region.

faq.q: Which Italy region suits a first destination wedding?
faq.a: It depends on the day you picture. Lake Como and the Amalfi Coast suit a villa wedding with water views, while Tuscany and Puglia suit a long weekend on one estate, as Cristina and Brett's and Jenayde and Alfonso's weddings show.

faq.q: Can you marry legally at an Italian villa?
faq.a: Our Italy legal guide explains that a symbolic ceremony has no legal standing in Italy. Confirm the requirements for your own passports with the marriage office (ufficio di stato civile) of your chosen comune or the Italian consulate. If you marry in Italy, Smartraveller notes you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, though in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia.

faq.q: Can we marry in Italy outside the summer months?
faq.a: The weddings on this page that state a date fall in June, September and autumn, and none confirms a winter date. If you are considering a winter date, check with your venue and your region guide first.

faq.q: Do multi-day Italy weddings work for travelling guests?
faq.a: They can. Cristina and Brett and Jenayde and Alfonso each held three days of events on one estate, from a welcome barbecue in Tuscany to a pool party in Puglia, and Tiara and Josh spread theirs over four days in Positano. Tiara's advice, as her page reports it, is that this took pressure off the wedding day.
